author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDx Talk, Dr. Natasha Latouf emphasizes the critical role of context in scientific research and the interpretation of evidence. Drawing on her own research on how to best find extraterrestrial life, she demonstrates how findings can be misleading or incomplete when the broader environmental, cultural, or situational context is overlooked. Dr. Latouf argues that meaningful inquiry, both scientific and in our everyday lives, requires us to consider contextual factors to produce accurate and reliable conclusions. 

Dr. Natasha Latouf, NASA Postdoctoral Program (NPP) Fellow, is a recent Ph.D. graduate from George Mason University studying astrobiology - the study of life on planets outside of our Solar System, known as exoplanets. Specifically, she studies the atmospheres of exoplanets to understand the requirements to detect indications of life on other worlds. Her full project is titled Bayesian Analysis for Remote Biosignature Identification on Earth, otherwise known as the BAR
title: How this next-gen telescope will search for life in space | Natasha Latouf | TEDxFoggyBottom
